ideal: Checker reads a fence that names a language as a block of the unit in whose own text it lies.
note: one sentence; the conditions become the subject's description

ideal:
A run exits with code 2 when any of these holds:
- some frontmatter lists a missing plugin
- checker reports that some document has a frontmatter it cannot read
- the run asks for a command that is not available
- the run gets code 2 from a plugin
note: the run leads; the first two conditions stay about any frontmatter or document

ideal: Checker reports a misaiming for every test the project declares that checks a unit that is not a claim.
Checker reports a misnesting for every miscited unit.

A unit is hidden exactly when it is a bug or a conflict and at least one of these holds:
- the project has a tracker and the unit names no issue
- the unit names an issue the tracker does not know
- the unit names an issue the tracker has closed
- it is a bug, the project has a runner, and it is not tested
- it is a conflict and it is not paired
note: the three shared conditions said once

ideal: The checker cannot read a circular frontmatter.
The checker cannot read a doubled frontmatter.
Checker reports a finding for every adrift test.
Checker never reads a fence that lies in a unit's own text as a block of a unit that sits in that unit.
note: never instead of a block of no unit

ideal: A run exits with code 1 when it gets code 1 from some plugin and code 2 from none.
Checker reports a freelancing for every spec that cites neither an axiom nor a spec.
Checker reports a rotting for every tag that names no unit.
When the project has a tracker, checker reports an untracking for every conflict that names no issue.
A frontmatter without a plugins key holds no entry.
note: without for is not a ... with

ideal: It must be possible that checker reports no finding for anything while a document holds an axiom, a spec that sits in that axiom, and an index that matches the document, and the project declares a test that carries a tag naming that spec.
note: the scene told as one sentence instead of a list of numbered names

ideal:
A unit is unfounded exactly when it is:
- a spec that cites neither an axiom nor a spec
- an exception that cites no spec, or no fact
- a bug that cites no spec
note: neither/nor and an elided second cites

ideal: A fence whose second word is vocabulary has the role of vocabulary.
Checker reports a misnesting for every exception that cites a unit that is neither a spec nor a fact.
A test checks a unit exactly when it carries a tag that names the unit.

A unit is miscited exactly when it is:
- an axiom that cites a unit that is not an axiom
- a spec that cites a unit that is not an axiom, a spec or a fact
- an exception that cites a unit that is neither a spec nor a fact
- a bug that cites a unit that is not a spec
- a fact, a conflict or a term that cites any unit
note: the three cites-anything kinds merged into one line

ideal: Checker reports no untesting for a tested claim.
Checker reports a misnesting for every term that cites a unit.
Checker does not run a plugin over a document that starts with a listing frontmatter that does not list the plugin, unless the command line of a run names the document.
note: the command-line exception said as unless

ideal: Checker reports an outdated tracking for every conflict that names an issue the tracker has closed.

If the author asks about leaving out any unit for a scenario that a search leaving one unit out requires to happen, the author also asks about leaving out, for that scenario, every unit the search leaves out.
note: no numbered unit names; any/every carries the two quantifiers

ideal:
A list can be put in a sentence exactly when:
- it has three clauses or fewer, and only items that are one clause
- if it has more than two clauses, it has no item that holds a comma
- it fits a line when it is put in a sentence
- no clause before its last begins with a time phrase or has a relative clause in it
note: the either/or said as an if; the two before-last rules merged

ideal: Checker reports a finding for every misleading test.
Checker reports a mistracking for every conflict that names an issue the tracker does not know.
When a run asks for a generate command, checker reports every handwritten statement of a unit, and if there is one, the run does not exit with code 0.
note: every and if there is one replace the three quantifiers

ideal: When the project has a tracker, checker reports an untracking for every bug that names no issue.
When it generates, checker never writes a handwritten statement of a unit.

For every document the project lists among the documents it checks, the analyzer is asked to hold the formula of each unit that a document of its context holds, when that unit holds a formula with no keyword.
note: two documents told apart by role, not by number

ideal: The formula of a unit cannot be said in words when it names a word that has no reading, or when the unit holds more than one formula.
When one unit shares a word with another, the analyzer is asked about the first together with the second.

When a search leaves one unit out and requires some scenario to happen, then for each unit it leaves out:
- the analyzer is asked to hold that unit's formula
- the search does not require that unit to hold
- the search requires every other unit whose formula the analyzer is asked to hold to hold
note: every other replaces the nested different-units condition

ideal: When the analyzer is asked about one unit together with another, the first is linked to the second through shared words.
When a run asks for a check command and checker reports the statement of some unit, the run does not exit with code 0.
note: some unit instead of a quantified unit

ideal: A search that leaves one unit out and requires a scenario to happen is asked after the first search is answered, and that scenario cannot happen while every held unit holds.
When it generates, checker writes the statement of a unit exactly when that statement is unwritten or stale.
note: the two implications said as exactly when
